```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Add Snowflake data to a Shiny app using each visitor's own account and role.
Query through a DBI connection, or use dbplyr to work with tables.

The example first shows the signed-in user's Snowflake username and role,
so you can check the connection before querying your data.

## Snowflake setup

Install `odbc` and the Snowflake ODBC driver. Ask your administrator for a
[custom-client OAuth integration](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/oauth-custom)
with `http://localhost:8100` as its redirect URI. Users need a role with
access to the warehouse and data.

For this local HTTP callback, the development integration needs
`OAUTH_ALLOW_NON_TLS_REDIRECT_URI = TRUE`. Use an HTTPS callback when
deploying. The [integration settings](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/create-security-integration-oauth-snowflake)
describe this option and refresh-token settings.

Save the integration's client ID and secret in a local `.Renviron` file,
then restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

## A complete app

Save this as `app.R`. Replace the connection settings, keeping the server
and role the same in the sign-in client and connection helper:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_snowflake_client(
  server = "organization-account.snowflakecomputing.com",
  role = "REPORTING_READER",
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_snowflake(
    auth$connection,
    server = "organization-account.snowflakecomputing.com",
    role = "REPORTING_READER",
    warehouse = "REPORTING_WH",
    database = "ANALYTICS"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER(), CURRENT_ROLE()")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)` from the app directory and open
`http://localhost:8100`. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the
output.

## Query a table

Replace the output expression with SQL for your data. For example, if your
table is `ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS`:

```{r table-query}
output$rows <- renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM ANALYTICS.PUBLIC.ORDERS LIMIT 20")
})
```

`con()` gets the current user's connection. Call it inside the render or
reactive expression before using DBI or dbplyr.

## Connection defaults

Set `schema = "PUBLIC"` on the helper to choose a default schema. Omit
`warehouse`, `database`, or `schema` to use the account's defaults.
If the installed ODBC driver has a different name, set `driver`.
See `?oauth_db_snowflake` for the full arguments.

## External OAuth

If Snowflake uses Entra, Okta, or another external provider for OAuth,
configure a shinyOAuth client for that provider. Request the audience and
role scopes accepted by your Snowflake integration.

Connect with `oauth_db_snowflake()` as above. Set `target` if your client
uses named token targets, and `required_scopes` to the integration's role
scope. For native Snowflake OAuth, the helper derives that scope from
`role`; external providers may use different scope names.
[Authentication and sessions](authorization.html) explains custom targets.
